title: TOEFL ITP - Section 2 Part B Written Expressions Questions
description: Preguntas para practicar la sección 2 parte B Expresión Escrita del TOEFL ITP.

questions.explanation: A → an: Antes de un sustantivo singular contable que se menciona por primera vez, se utiliza el artículo indefinido. La expresión correcta es an important exhibition.
questions.sentence: The Armory Show, held in New York in 1913, was a important exhibition of modern European art.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Armory Show, **<u>held</u>** in New York in 1913, was **<u>a</u>** important **<u>exhibition</u>** of **<u>modern</u>** European art.

questions.explanation: At rate → at a rate: Antes de un sustantivo singular contable usado de manera general se necesita un artículo. La expresión correcta es «grows at a rate of...»
questions.sentence: Human hair grows at rate of about one-half to one inch a month.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Human hair grows **<u>at rate</u>** of **<u>about</u>** one-half **<u>to</u>** one inch **<u>a</u>** month.

questions.explanation: A → an: Antes de un sustantivo singular contable que aparece por primera vez, se requiere un artículo indefinido. La estructura correcta es «an intricate aquatic community», porque intricate comienza con sonido vocal.
questions.sentence: A coral reef, a intricate aquatic community of plants and animals, is found only in warm, shallow, sunlit seas.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A coral reef, **<u>a</u>** intricate aquatic **<u>community</u>** of plants and animals, is **<u>found</u>** only in **<u>warm</u>**, shallow, sunlit seas.

questions.explanation: The nitrogen → nitrogen: Los nombres de sustancias en sentido general normalmente no llevan artículo. La forma correcta es «Nitrogen makes up over 78 percent of the Earth's atmosphere».
questions.sentence: The nitrogen makes up over 78 percent of the Earth's atmosphere, the gaseous mass surrounding the planet.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>The nitrogen</u>** makes up **<u>over</u>** 78 **<u>percent of</u>** the Earth's atmosphere, the gaseous mass **<u>surrounding</u>** the planet.

questions.explanation: As small → a small: Después del verbo «begin», cuando se describe cómo inicia algo, se necesita un artículo antes de un sustantivo contable singular. La estructura correcta es «begins as a small, clear stream».
questions.sentence: The Mississippi, the longest river in the United States, begins as small, clear stream in northwestern Minnesota
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Mississippi, the **<u>longest</u>** river in the United States, begins **<u>as small</u>**, **<u>clear</u>** stream in **<u>northwestern</u>** Minnesota

questions.explanation: A → an: Se usa an antes de palabras que comienzan con sonido vocálico.
questions.sentence: In the United States, Maryland ranks second only to Virginia as a oyster-producing state.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>In</u>** the United States, Maryland ranks **<u>second</u>** only **<u>to</u>** Virginia as **<u>a</u>** oyster-producing state.

questions.explanation: And rest → and the rest: Se necesita el artículo definido antes de rest porque se refiere a una parte específica del sistema solar.
questions.sentence: The Milky Way galaxy includes the Sun, its planets, and rest of the solar system, along with billions of stars and other objects.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Milky Way galaxy **<u>includes</u>** the Sun, its planets, **<u>and rest</u>** of the solar system, along with **<u>billions</u>** of stars and **<u>other objects</u>**.

questions.explanation: In world → in the world: Se necesita el artículo the para referirse al mundo como concepto único.
questions.sentence: The first national park in world, Yellowstone National Park, was established in 1872.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The **<u>first</u>** national park **<u>in world</u>**, Yellowstone National Park, **<u>was</u>** established **<u>in</u>** 1872.

questions.explanation: A → the: Se habla del primer estado específico en una lista histórica, por eso se usa the first state.
questions.sentence: On December 7, 1787, Delaware became a first state to ratify the United States Constitution.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>On</u>** December 7, 1787, Delaware **<u>became</u>** **<u>a</u>** first state **<u>to ratify</u>** the United States Constitution.

questions.explanation: A greenish → greenish: Water es incontable y no requiere artículo indefinido en este contexto.
questions.sentence: Decaying plant matter may be responsible for a yellow or brown color, while algae may cause a greenish water.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Decaying</u>** plant **<u>matter</u>** may be responsible for a yellow **<u>or brown</u>** color, while algae may cause **<u>a greenish</u>** water.

questions.explanation: Sun → the sun: El sustantivo contable en singular «sun» necesita un artículo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «sun» por «the sun».
questions.sentence: Every year during the fall and spring, sun emits broadband noise that overpowers broadcast signals.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Every year during **<u>the</u>** fall and spring, **<u>sun</u>** emits broadband noise **<u>that</u>** **<u>overpowers</u>** broadcast signals.

questions.explanation: A → an: Se utiliza el artículo «a» delante de la palabra «abolitionist», que empieza por un sonido vocálico. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «a» por «an».
questions.sentence: John Brown, a abolitionist, led a group of about 20 men in a raid on Harper's Ferry before the Civil War.
questions.sentenceFormatted: John Brown, **<u>a</u>** abolitionist, **<u>led</u>** **<u>a</u>** group of about 20 men in a raid on Harper's Ferry before **<u>the</u>** Civil War.

questions.explanation: A → the: El artículo indefinido «a» se utiliza con el sustantivo «cause». Se trata de un sustantivo propio, por lo que debe emplearse el artículo propio. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «a» por «the».
questions.sentence: Suicide is a fastest growing cause of death in young people in the United States.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Suicide</u>** **<u>is</u>** **<u>a</u>** fastest growing cause of death in **<u>young people</u>** in the United States.

questions.explanation: An → a: El artículo «An» se utiliza delante de la palabra «health», que comienza con un sonido consonántico. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «An» por «A».
questions.sentence: An health expert says that there is no known safe level of lead exposure, especially for children under the age of six.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>An</u>** health expert **<u>says</u>** that there is **<u>no</u>** known safe level of lead exposure, especially for children under **<u>the</u>** age of six.

questions.explanation: About a → about: El artículo definido «a» se utiliza con el sustantivo «people», que está en plural. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «about a» por «about».
questions.sentence: In 1995, about a 3.9 million people were born in the United States.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In 1995, **<u>about a</u>** 3.9 **<u>million</u>** people **<u>were</u>** born in **<u>the</u>** United States.

questions.explanation: Is → is a: El sustantivo contable en singular «park» necesita un artículo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «is» por «is a».
questions.sentence: Knott's Berry Farm is family-run theme park that evolved from a fried chicken restaurant into a $120 million per year attraction.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Knott's Berry Farm **<u>is</u>** family-run theme park that **<u>evolved</u>** **<u>from</u>** a fried chicken restaurant **<u>into</u>** a $120 million per year attraction.

questions.explanation: AIDS → The AIDS: El sustantivo singular contable «virus» requiere un artículo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «AIDS» por «The AIDS».
questions.sentence: AIDS virus now ranks with tuberculosis and malaria as the world's deadliest infectious diseases.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>AIDS</u>** virus now ranks with **<u>tuberculosis</u>** and malaria as **<u>the</u>** world's deadliest **<u>infectious</u>** diseases.

questions.explanation: The → a: El artículo definido «the» se utiliza con el sustantivo «widow». Este sustantivo no es específico, por lo que debe emplearse el artículo indefinido. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «the» por «a».
questions.sentence: In 1901, Anna Edson Taylor, the 43-year-old widow, became the first person to survive going over Niagara Falls in a barrel.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In 1901, Anna Edson Taylor, **<u>the</u>** 43-year-old widow, **<u>became</u>** **<u>the</u>** first person to survive going over Niagara Falls in **<u>a</u>** barrel.

questions.explanation: A heavy → the heavy: El artículo definido «a» se utiliza con el sustantivo plural «rains». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «a heavy» por «the heavy».
questions.sentence: With a heavy winter rains almost here, slugs and snails will be coming out of their summer sleep.
questions.sentenceFormatted: With **<u>a heavy</u>** winter rains almost **<u>here</u>**, slugs and snails **<u>will be</u>** coming out of **<u>their</u>** summer sleep.

questions.explanation: Lesser → less: Para formar el grado comparativo de los adjetivos largos, se utiliza less + adjective. La estructura correcta es less elaborate than, que significa "menos elaboradas que".
questions.sentence: The public ceremonies of the Plains Indians are lesser elaborate than those of the Navajo in the Southwest.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The **<u>public ceremonies</u>** of the Plains Indians are **<u>lesser</u>** elaborate **<u>than those</u>** of **<u>the</u>** Navajo in the Southwest.

questions.explanation: Most lowest → lowest: Los adjetivos most y -est no se utilizan juntos. Para expresar el grado máximo, debe elegirse una sola forma: the lowest temperature.
questions.sentence: Basal body temperature refers to the most lowest temperature of a healthy individual during waking hours.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Basal body temperature **<u>refers</u>** to the **<u>most lowest</u>** temperature of a **<u>healthy</u>** individual **<u>during</u>** waking hours.

questions.explanation: That than → than that: La comparación correcta es longer than that of a duck. El pronombre demostrativo that sustituye al sustantivo repetido (the neck). No se utiliza than of.
questions.sentence: A goose's neck is a little longer that than of a duck, and not so gracefully curved as a swan's.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A goose's neck is **<u>a little</u>** longer **<u>that than</u>** of a duck, **<u>and not</u>** so **<u>gracefully</u>** curved as a swan's.

questions.explanation: Easy → easier. La estructura de comparación requiere un comparativo porque se compara ir con el viento y contra el viento: it is much easier to go with the wind than against it.
questions.sentence: Anyone rowing a boat in a strong wind knows it is much easy to go with the wind than against it.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Anyone</u>** rowing a boat **<u>in a strong wind</u>** knows it is much **<u>easy</u>** to go with the wind than **<u>against it</u>**.

questions.explanation: And → but: Cuando dos elementos cumplen la misma función sintáctica, deben unirse con una estructura paralela. La expresión correcta es not in war but through diplomacy, manteniendo el paralelismo entre ambas partes de la comparación.
questions.sentence: Matthew C. Perry, a United States naval commander, gained fame not in war and through diplomacy
questions.sentenceFormatted: Matthew C. Perry, a United States **<u>naval</u>** commander, **<u>gained</u>** fame not in war **<u>and</u>** through **<u>diplomacy</u>**

questions.explanation: Denser → dense: La estructura correcta es less dense than; no se duplica el comparativo.
questions.sentence: Ice is less denser than the liquid from which it is formed.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Ice is less **<u>denser</u>** **<u>than</u>** the liquid **<u>from which</u>** **<u>it</u>** is formed.

questions.explanation: More strong → stronger: La forma comparativa de «more strong» está mal construida. El comparativo de un adjetivo corto se forma con {-er}. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «more strong» por «stronger».
questions.sentence: The silk cords which make up a spider's web are three times more strong than the same size cord of iron.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The silk cords which **<u>make up</u>** a spider's web are three times **<u>more strong</u>** than **<u>the same</u>** size cord **<u>of iron</u>**.

questions.explanation: Most than → more than: «Than» debería ir precedido del comparativo «more». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «most than» por «more than».
questions.sentence: The giant sequoia, which can grow to most than 300 feet tall, is the largest living thing on planet Earth.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The giant sequoia, **<u>which can</u>** grow to **<u>most than</u>** 300 feet tall, is **<u>the largest</u>** living **<u>thing</u>** on planet Earth.

questions.explanation: Great → greater: Esta frase incluye «than», pero le falta la primera parte del comparativo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «great» por «greater».
questions.sentence: The electric eel is not unique in its ability to generate electricity, but the electric eel can generate a great electric current than any other electric fish.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The electric eel is **<u>not unique</u>** in **<u>its</u>** ability to generate electricity, but the electric eel can generate a **<u>great</u>** electric current than **<u>any other</u>** electric fish.

questions.explanation: Massivest → massive: El superlativo «the...most massivest...» está mal formado. «Most» no se puede usar con «-est». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «massivest» por «massive».
questions.sentence: The iron core and the rocky mantle and crust are the Earth's most massivest constituents.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The iron **<u>core and</u>** the rocky mantle and crust **<u>are</u>** the Earth's most **<u>massivest</u>** **<u>constituents</u>**.

questions.explanation: Workablest → workable: La forma del superlativo «workablest» es incorrecta. El superlativo de un adjetivo largo se forma con «most». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «workablest» por «most workable».
questions.sentence: One of Thomas Edison's attempted inventions that was definitely not among his workablest ideas was a sewing machine powered by the sound of the human voice.
questions.sentenceFormatted: One of Thomas Edison's attempted inventions that was definitely not **<u>among</u>** his **<u>workablest</u>** ideas was a sewing machine **<u>powered by</u>** the sound of the **<u>human voice</u>**.

questions.explanation: Either → neither: La conjunción de disyunción correcta es «ni... ni». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «Either» por «Neither».
questions.sentence: Either niobium nor tantalum is mined in the United States.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Either</u>** niobium nor **<u>tantalum</u>** **<u>is mined</u>** **<u>in</u>** the United States.

questions.explanation: Or → and: La conjunción de coordinación correcta es «tanto... como». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «or» por «and».
questions.sentence: The Golden Gate Bridge is designed both to sway as much as 28 feet or to rise and fall as much as 16 feet.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Golden Gate Bridge is **<u>designed</u>** both to sway as **<u>much</u>** as 28 feet **<u>or</u>** to rise and fall as much as 16 **<u>feet</u>**.

questions.explanation: Which apparently → apparently serves: El pronombre which está demás. Para corregir debemos solo eliminar para respetar la estructura en paralelo del verbo en presente.
questions.sentence: The male cicada sound is made by specialized structures on the abdomen and which apparently serves to attract females.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The male cicada **<u>sound</u>** is made **<u>by specialized structures</u>** on the abdomen and **<u>which apparently</u>** serves **<u>to attract</u>** females.

questions.explanation: Damaging → damage: El participio presente «damaging» no está en paralelo con el verbo «trample». La conjunción «either... or» indica que deberían estar en paralelo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «damaging» por «damage».*
questions.sentence: Goats either trample the vegetation that Galapagos tortoises eat or damaging the canopies of the trees that protect the tortoises from the sun.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Goats **<u>either</u>** trample the vegetation that Galapagos tortoises eat or **<u>damaging</u>** the **<u>canopies</u>** of the trees that protect the **<u>tortoises</u>** from the sun.

questions.explanation: To → from: La expresión fija es from species to species, utilizada para indicar variación entre diferentes especies. La preposición correcta es from.
questions.sentence: The importance of environmental stimuli in the development of coordination between sensory input and motor response varies to species to species.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The **<u>importance</u>** of environmental stimuli in **<u>the</u>** development of coordination between sensory input **<u>and</u>** motor response varies **<u>to</u>** species to species.

questions.explanation: To → at: Después del verbo found, cuando se indica la ubicación de un lugar o edificio, se utiliza la preposición at. La estructura correcta es found at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
questions.sentence: One of the most impressive collections of nineteenth-century European paintings in the United States can be found to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
questions.sentenceFormatted: One of the most impressive **<u>collections</u>** of nineteenth-century European **<u>paintings</u>** in the United States **<u>can</u>** be found **<u>to</u>** the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

questions.explanation: At → In: Para años específicos se usa la preposición in, no at. La estructura correcta es In 1939, television programs were being broadcast...
questions.sentence: At 1939, television programs were being broadcast in the United States, and the World's Fair of that year featured demonstrations of this advance in technology.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>At</u>** 1939, television **<u>programs</u>** were being broadcast in the United States, **<u>and</u>** the World's Fair of that year **<u>featured</u>** demonstrations of this advance in technology.

questions.explanation: Out the → out of the: La expresión correcta es pull something out of something, que significa "sacar algo de algo". La frase correcta es: pull the United States out of the Great Depression.
questions.sentence: The New Deal was President Franklin D. Roosevelt's program to pull the United States out the Great Depression in the 1930's.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The New Deal **<u>was</u>** President Franklin D. Roosevelt's **<u>program</u>** **<u>to pull</u>** the United States **<u>out the</u>** Great Depression in the 1930's.

questions.explanation: Between → from: La estructura correcta es admitting sunlight from outer space para indicar origen.
questions.sentence: The Earth’s atmosphere functions much like a giant greenhouse, admitting sunlight between outer space but preventing heat from escaping.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Earth’s atmosphere **<u>functions</u>** much like a giant greenhouse, admitting sunlight **<u>between</u>** outer space **<u>but</u>** preventing heat from **<u>escaping</u>**.

questions.explanation: Of → From: Para expresar un período de tiempo se usa From 1901 to 1914, no Of.
questions.sentence: Of 1901 to 1914, acclaimed actor Douglas Fairbanks appeared on stage in a series of light comedies.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Of</u>** 1901 to 1914, acclaimed actor Douglas Fairbanks appeared on **<u>stage</u>** in **<u>a series</u>** of light **<u>comedies</u>**.

questions.explanation: Stands → stands for: Se ha omitido una preposición en la expresión «stands». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «stands» por «stands for».
questions.sentence: The abbreviation A.M. stands ante meridian, which is Latin for "before noon."
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>The</u>** abbreviation A.M. **<u>stands</u>** ante meridian, **<u>which</u>** is Latin **<u>for</u>** "before noon."

questions.explanation: On → in: En el contexto de la música se utiliza incorrectamente la preposición «On». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «On» por «In».
questions.sentence: On music, when two notes are played together, they create harmony; but when three or more notes are played together, they form a chord.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>On</u>** music, when two notes are played **<u>together</u>**, they create harmony; but when three **<u>or</u>** more notes are played together, they **<u>form</u>** a chord.

questions.explanation: Of old → old: La expresión fija para indicar la edad es ...years old. En este caso, la forma correcta es from four to eighteen years old.
questions.sentence: In 1852 Massachusetts passed a law requiring all children from four to eighteen years of old to attend school.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In 1852 Massachusetts passed a law **<u>requiring</u>** all **<u>children</u>** from four **<u>to</u>** eighteen years **<u>of old</u>** to attend school.

questions.explanation: What → that: En una cláusula adjetiva se necesita un pronombre relativo que funcione como sujeto. La estructura correcta es «Light rays that enter the eye...». «That» introduce una cláusula relativa y sustituye al sustantivo anterior «light rays».
questions.sentence: Light rays what enter the eye must be focused onto a point on the retina In order for a clear visual image to form.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Light rays **<u>what</u>** enter the eye **<u>must</u>** be focused onto a point on the retina In order for a **<u>clear</u>** visual image **<u>to form</u>**.

questions.explanation: Hers → her: Antes de un sustantivo, debe utilizarse un adjetivo posesivo. Como los sujetos pertenecen a Margaret Mead, la forma correcta es «her subjects».
questions.sentence: Margaret Mead studied many different cultures and she was one of the first anthropologists to photograph hers subjects.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Margaret Mead **<u>studied</u>** many **<u>different</u>** cultures and she was one **<u>of the first</u>** anthropologists to photograph **<u>hers</u>** subjects.

questions.explanation: Who → which: Cuando el antecedente es una cosa «the laws of motion», el pronombre relativo correcto es «which», no «who», ya que «who» solo se utiliza para personas.
questions.sentence: Underlying aerodynamics and all other branches of theoretical mechanics are the laws of motion who were developed in the seventeenth century.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Underlying aerodynamics and **<u>all</u>** other **<u>branches</u>** of theoretical mechanics **<u>are</u>** the laws of motion **<u>who</u>** were developed in the seventeenth century.

questions.explanation: Who → which: Cuando el antecedente es una cosa «a place», el pronombre relativo correcto es «that» o «which», no «who», ya que «who» solo se utiliza para personas.
questions.sentence: Ripe fruit is often stored in a place who contains much carbon dioxide so that the fruit will not decay too rapidly.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Ripe</u>** fruit is often **<u>stored</u>** in a place **<u>who</u>** contains much carbon dioxide so that the fruit will not decay too **<u>rapidly</u>**.

questions.explanation: Another → other: La expresión fija es «each other», utilizada para indicar una relación recíproca entre dos o más elementos. La forma correcta es to «each other».
questions.sentence: The main purpose of classifying animals is to show the most probable evolutionary relationship of the different species to each another.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The main purpose of **<u>classifying</u>** animals **<u>is</u>** to show the most probable evolutionary relationship of the **<u>different</u>** species to each **<u>another</u>**.

questions.explanation: Another → other: Después de living se necesita un sustantivo plural; other living things es la estructura correcta.
questions.sentence: Bacteria are one of the most abundant life forms on Earth, growing on and inside another living things, in every type of environment.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Bacteria are one of the most **<u>abundant</u>** life **<u>forms</u>** on Earth, growing on and inside **<u>another</u>** living things, in every type of **<u>environment</u>**.

questions.explanation: Their → its: Cornea es singular, por lo que requiere el adjetivo posesivo its.
questions.sentence: Because it does not have a blood supply, the cornea takes their oxygen directly from the air.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Because</u>** it does not have a blood **<u>supply</u>**, the cornea takes **<u>their</u>** oxygen **<u>directly</u>** from the air.

questions.explanation: Hers → her: Antes de un sustantivo (plane) se usa un adjetivo posesivo, no un pronombre posesivo.
questions.sentence: While attempting to fly hers plane around the world in 1937, Amelia Earhart mysteriously disappeared.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>While</u>** attempting to fly **<u>hers</u>** plane **<u>around</u>** the world in 1937, Amelia Earhart **<u>mysteriously</u>** disappeared.

questions.explanation: It → they: El antecedente black holes es plural, por lo que el pronombre debe ser plural.
questions.sentence: Supermassive black holes are assumed to reside in the cores of most galaxies, and it play a key role in current models of how galaxies have formed over the past billions of years.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Supermassive black holes are **<u>assumed</u>** to reside in the cores of **<u>most</u>** galaxies, and **<u>it</u>** play a key role in current models of **<u>how</u>** galaxies have formed over the past billions of years.

questions.explanation: They → their: Antes del sustantivo colorful bodies se requiere un adjetivo posesivo.
questions.sentence: Many people are now using harlequin shrimps as pets because of they colorful bodies, but future pet owners need to be aware that these shrimps are very sensitive.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Many people are **<u>now</u>** using harlequin shrimps as pets because of **<u>they</u>** colorful bodies, but future **<u>pet</u>** owners need to be aware that these **<u>shrimps</u>** are very sensitive.

questions.explanation: Another → another living creature: Another debe modificar un sustantivo singular; la estructura debe mantener concordancia.
questions.sentence: Certain insects lay their eggs inside another living creatures in order that they might eat the creature from inside.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Certain insects lay their eggs inside **<u>another</u>** living creatures **<u>in order that</u>** they **<u>might</u>** eat the creature from **<u>inside</u>**.

questions.explanation: Them → they: El pronombre de objeto «them» no se utiliza antes del verbo «do not». Se requiere un pronombre de sujeto antes de un verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «them» por «they».
questions.sentence: Giraffes are sociable and prefer to live in groups, but them do not form permanent herds.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Giraffes are **<u>sociable</u>** and prefer to live in groups, but **<u>them</u>** do not **<u>form</u>** permanent **<u>herds</u>**.

questions.explanation: They → them: El pronombre sujeto «they» se utiliza después del verbo en infinitivo «to assist». Después de un infinitivo es obligatorio utilizar un pronombre de objeto. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «they» por «them».

questions.explanation: Forms → that forms: El sustantivo y el verbo «one forms» no son paralelos al sustantivo y a la oración adjetiva «snowflake that forms». questions.sentence: A snowflake that forms rapidly has more crystals than one forms slowly.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A snowflake **<u>that</u>** forms **<u>rapidly</u>** has **<u>more</u>** crystals than one **<u>forms</u>** slowly.

questions.explanation: During → from: La expresión fija es from... until... para indicar un período que se extiende desde un momento inicial hasta otro final. La forma correcta es from the 1920s until the present day.
questions.sentence: One of the problems of United States agriculture that has persisted during the 1920’s until the present day is the tendency of farm income to lag behind the costs of production.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>One of the problems</u>** of United States agriculture that has persisted **<u>during the</u>** 1920’s until the present day is the tendency of farm income to lag **<u>behind</u>** the costs of **<u>production</u>**.

questions.explanation: Work which → work for which: La expresión fija es be known for. Después de known, se utiliza la preposición for, como en The work for which the poet Emma Lazarus is best known....
questions.sentence: The work which the poet Emma Lazarus is best known is “The New Colossus,” which is inscribed on the pedestal of the Statue of Liberty.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The **<u>work which</u>** the **<u>poet</u>** Emma Lazarus is best known is “The New Colossus,” which **<u>is inscribed</u>** on the pedestal **<u>of</u>** the Statue of Liberty.

questions.explanation: Associated by → associated with: Para formar la voz pasiva, se utiliza la estructura be + participio pasado. La expresión correcta es is associated with, donde associated es el participio pasado y with completa la expresión fija.
questions.sentence: Sleep is controlled by the brain and associated by characteristic breathing rhythms.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Sleep is **<u>controlled</u>** by **<u>the brain</u>** and **<u>associated by</u>** characteristic **<u>breathing</u>** rhythms.

questions.explanation: About → with: La expresión correcta es be credited with + gerundio, que significa "ser reconocido por hacer algo". La estructura correcta es is credited with greatly furthering the cause...
questions.sentence: The strongly patriotic character of Charles Sangster's poetry is credited about greatly furthering the cause of confederation in Canada.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The strongly **<u>patriotic</u>** character of Charles Sangster's poetry **<u>is credited</u>** **<u>about</u>** greatly **<u>furthering</u>** the cause of confederation in Canada.

questions.explanation: Black a → black with a: Se ha omitido una preposición en la expresión «mix black». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «black a» por «black with a».
questions.sentence: One of the techniques used in art is to mix black a color to produce a shade and to mix white with a color to produce a tint.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>One of</u>** the techniques used **<u>in art</u>** is to mix **<u>black a</u>** color to produce **<u>a shade</u>** and to mix white with a color to produce a tint.

questions.explanation: At → by: Se ha utilizado la preposición incorrecta «at» con «called». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «at» por «by».
questions.sentence: The place where the name of a newspaper is printed along with the date and the price is called at the term "banner."
questions.sentenceFormatted: The place where the **<u>name of</u>** a newspaper is printed **<u>along with</u>** the date and the price **<u>is</u>** called **<u>at</u>** the term "banner."

questions.explanation: Shape the → shape of the: Se ha omitido una preposición en la expresión «shape the container». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «shape the» por «shape of the».
questions.sentence: A liquid takes up a fixed amount of space but has no shape of its own and so takes the shape the container into which it is poured.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A liquid takes up a fixed amount of space but **<u>has no</u>** shape of **<u>its own</u>** and so takes the **<u>shape the</u>** container **<u>into which</u>** it is poured.

questions.explanation: As → for. La estructura paralela correcta es used as a drying oil ... and for making linoleum. Después de used se utiliza for + gerundio para expresar propósito.
questions.sentence: Linseed oil is used as a drying oil in paints and varnishes and as making linoleum, oilcloth, and certain inks.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Linseed oil is used as a **<u>drying</u>** oil in **<u>paints</u>** and varnishes and **<u>as</u>** making linoleum, oilcloth, and **<u>certain</u>** inks.

questions.explanation: Are called → that arecalled: La oración necesita una cláusula relativa para describir «hollow teeth». La estructura correcta es «hollow teeth that are called fangs», donde that introduce la información adicional sobre los dientes.
questions.sentence: Some snakes have hollow teeth are called fangs that they use to poison their victims.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Some</u>** snakes have hollow teeth **<u>are called</u>** fangs that they **<u>use</u>** to poison **<u>their</u>** victims.

questions.explanation: Its → their: El adjetivo posesivo debe concordar con el sustantivo al que hace referencia. Como el antecedente es «seismic waves» (plural), corresponde utilizar «their point of origin».
questions.sentence: A seismograph records oscillation of the ground caused by seismic waves, vibrations that travel from its point of origin through the Earth or along its surface.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A seismograph records oscillation of the ground **<u>caused by</u>** seismic waves, vibrations that **<u>travel</u>** from **<u>its</u>** point of origin **<u>through</u>** the Earth or along its surface.

questions.explanation: Which it still → which still: El pronombre relativo «which» ya funciona como sujeto de la cláusula relativa. No debe añadirse otro pronombre «it».
questions.sentence: Rice, which it still forms the staple diet of much of the world’s population, grows best in hot, wetlands.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Rice, **<u>which it still</u>** forms the staple diet of **<u>much</u>** of the world’s population, grows **<u>best</u>** in **<u>hot</u>**, wetlands.

questions.explanation: Renamed it → renamed: El verbo «rename» ya incluye el objeto directo. No se necesita el pronombre «it» después del verbo porque «what is now San Francisco» funciona como el objeto renombrado.
questions.sentence: Founded by the Spanish as Yerba Buena in 1835, what is now San Francisco was taken over by the United States in 1846 and later renamed it.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Founded by</u>** the Spanish **<u>as</u>** Yerba Buena in 1835, what is now San Francisco **<u>was taken</u>** over by the United States in 1846 and later **<u>renamed it</u>**.

questions.explanation: He composed → composed: No se necesita un segundo sujeto; la estructura correcta es un participio o una cláusula independiente.
questions.sentence: John Rosamond Johnson he composed numerous songs, including Lift Every Voice and Sing, for which his brother, James Weldon Johnson, wrote the words.
questions.sentenceFormatted: John Rosamond Johnson **<u>he composed</u>** numerous **<u>songs</u>**, **<u>including</u>** Lift Every Voice and Sing, **<u>for which</u>** his brother, James Weldon Johnson, wrote the words.

questions.explanation: Which → whose: Se necesita un pronombre posesivo para indicar que las obras pertenecen al arquitecto.
questions.sentence: Minoru Yamasaki achieved a reputation as an architect which works departed from the austerity frequently associated with architecture after the Second World War.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Minoru Yamasaki achieved a reputation as an architect **<u>which</u>** works **<u>departed from</u>** the austerity **<u>frequently</u>** associated **<u>with</u>** architecture after the Second World War.

questions.explanation: We → us: El pronombre sujeto «we» se utiliza después de la preposición «toward». Después de una preposición es necesario un pronombre de objeto. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «we» por «us».
questions.sentence: The moon does not rotate on an axis, so it appears with the same face always turned toward we.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The moon does not **<u>rotate</u>** on an axis, so it appears **<u>with</u>** the same face **<u>always</u>** turned toward **<u>we</u>**.

questions.explanation: We → us: El pronombre sujeto «we» se utiliza después del verbo «enables». Después de un verbo es obligatorio utilizar un pronombre de objeto. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «we» por «us».
questions.sentence: The fact that the density of our bodies is relatively less than that of water enables we to float.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The fact that **<u>the density</u>** of our bodies **<u>is</u>** relatively less than **<u>that of</u>** water enables **<u>we</u>** to float.

questions.explanation: Its → their: El adjetivo posesivo en singular «its» se refiere al sustantivo plural «airliners». Un adjetivo posesivo debe concordar con el sustantivo al que se refiere. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «its» por «their».
questions.sentence: Commercial airliners do not fly in the vicinity of volcanic eruptions because even a small amount of volcanic ash can damage its engines.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Commercial airliners do not fly **<u>in the vicinity</u>** of volcanic eruptions because even a small **<u>amount</u>** of volcanic **<u>ash</u>** can damage **<u>its</u>** engines.

questions.explanation: He → him: El pronombre sujeto «he» se utiliza después del verbo «depicting». Después de un verbo es obligatorio utilizar un pronombre de objeto. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «he» por «him».
questions.sentence: A commemorative stamp honoring Chuck Yeager, the pilot who broke the sound barrier in 1947, was issued depicting he and the X-15 jet that he flew.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A commemorative stamp **<u>honoring</u>** Chuck Yeager, the pilot **<u>who</u>** broke the sound barrier in 1947, was issued depicting **<u>he</u>** and the X-15 jet that **<u>he</u>** flew.

questions.explanation: Density → densities: Después de la expresión «one of the», el sustantivo debe ir en plural. La estructura correcta es «one of the lowest population densities».
questions.sentence: Because of its vast tracts of virtually uninhabited northern forest, Canada has one of the lowest population density in the world.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Because of **<u>its</u>** vast tracts of **<u>virtually</u>** uninhabited northern forest, Canada has **<u>one</u>** of the lowest population **<u>density</u>** in the world.

questions.explanation: Setting → settings: Cuando se habla de categorías generales, el sustantivo debe ir en plural. La expresión correcta es «geological settings».
questions.sentence: Volcanism occurs on Earth in several geological setting, most of which are associated with the boundaries of the enormous, rigid plates that make up the lithosphere
questions.sentenceFormatted: Volcanism **<u>occurs</u>** on Earth in several geological **<u>setting</u>**, most of which are associated with the boundaries of the **<u>enormous</u>**, rigid plates that **<u>make up</u>** the lithosphere

questions.explanation: Fabrics → fabric: Cuando un número o una cantidad mayor que uno modifica un sustantivo contable, este debe ir en plural. La expresión correcta es «as much fabric», «fabric» es incontable; en este contexto debe usarse la forma adecuada según el significado «as much fabric».
questions.sentence: Today modern textile mills can manufacture as much fabrics in a few seconds as it once took workers weeks to produce by hand.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Today modern textile mills can manufacture as much **<u>fabrics</u>** in **<u>a few</u>** seconds as it once took **<u>workers</u>** weeks **<u>to produce</u>** by hand.

questions.explanation: Object → objects: Después de un número mayor que uno, el sustantivo contable debe ir en plural. La expresión correcta es «old objects».
questions.sentence: Antique collecting became a significant pastime in the 1800's when old object began to be appreciated for their beauty as well as for their historical importance.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Antique collecting **<u>became</u>** a significant pastime in the 1800's **<u>when</u>** old **<u>object</u>** began to be **<u>appreciated for</u>** their beauty as well as for their historical importance.

questions.explanation: Automobile → automobiles: Cuando se habla de un producto o material en sentido general, se utiliza un sustantivo singular. La expresión correcta es «the manufacture of automobiles» o «automobile manufacturing», según el contexto; aquí el error es usar «automobile» donde se requiere la forma plural.
questions.sentence: The manufacture of automobile was extremely expensive until assembly-line techniques made them cheaper to produce.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The manufacture of **<u>automobile</u>** was **<u>extremely</u>** expensive **<u>until</u>** assembly-line techniques **<u>made</u>** them cheaper to produce.

questions.explanation: Lived large → lived in large: Después del verbo live, cuando significa "habitar", no puede ir seguido directamente de un sustantivo. Se necesita una preposición «lived in large multilevel structures».
questions.sentence: The Hopi, the westernmost tribe of Pueblo Indians, have traditionally lived large multilevel structures clustered in towns.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Hopi, the westernmost **<u>tribe of</u>** Pueblo Indians, have **<u>traditionally</u>** **<u>lived large</u>** multilevel structures clustered in **<u>towns</u>**.

questions.explanation: Of holding → to hold its shape (estructura correcta). Después de able se utiliza to + infinitive.
questions.sentence: Composed of heavy-textured clay soil, adobe has great elasticity when moist, but when dry is able of holding its shape.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Composed of</u>** heavy-textured clay **<u>soil</u>**, adobe **<u>has</u>** great elasticity when moist, but when dry is able **<u>of holding</u>** its shape.

questions.explanation: Lived → living: Se necesita un participio presente que funcione como adjetivo para describir a las bacterias «Bacteria living in the soil...». La forma lived indicaría una acción pasada terminada, lo cual no corresponde al significado.
questions.sentence: Bacteria lived in the soil play a vital role in recycling the carbon and nitrogen needed by plants
questions.sentenceFormatted: Bacteria **<u>lived</u>** in the soil play a **<u>vital role</u>** **<u>in recycling</u>** the carbon and nitrogen **<u>needed</u>** by plants

questions.explanation: Pear-shaping → pear-shaped: El adjetivo activo «pear-shaping» se utiliza para describir el sustantivo «huevos». Se necesita un adjetivo pasivo para que el significado sea lógico. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «pear-shaping» por «pear-shaped».
questions.sentence: The guillemot's pear-shaping eggs spin when they are bumped, which prevents them from rolling off the bare cliff ledges on which they are laid.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The guillemot's **<u>pear-shaping</u>** eggs spin when they are **<u>bumped</u>**, which prevents them from **<u>rolling</u>** off the bare cliff ledges on which they are **<u>laid</u>**.

questions.explanation: Signaled → signaling: El adjetivo pasivo «Signaled» se utiliza para describir el sustantivo «butterflies». Se necesita un adjetivo activo para que el significado sea lógico. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «Signaled» por «Signaling».
questions.sentence: Signaled male butterflies attract female butterflies with flashes of ultraviolet light that sparkle off their flapping wings.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Signaled</u>** male butterflies attract female butterflies with **<u>flashes</u>** of ultraviolet light **<u>that</u>** sparkle off their **<u>flapping</u>** wings.

questions.explanation: Transforms → transform: El sujeto cells es plural, por lo que el verbo debe estar en forma plural.
questions.sentence: Metabolism is the inclusive term for the chemical reactions by which the cells of an organism transforms energy, maintain their identity, and reproduce.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Metabolism is the **<u>inclusive</u>** term for the **<u>chemical</u>** reactions **<u>by which</u>** the cells of an organism **<u>transforms</u>** energy, maintain their identity, and reproduce.

questions.explanation: Had → have: Después de may se usa el verbo en forma base: may have been.
questions.sentence: Cumulative evidence shows that during the ancient Noachian time period, the surface environment of Mars had liquid water and may had been habitable for microorganisms.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Cumulative evidence shows **<u>that</u>** during the ancient Noachian time **<u>period</u>**, the surface environment of Mars **<u>had</u>** liquid water and may had been **<u>habitable</u>** for microorganisms.

questions.explanation: Produce → produces: El sujeto «the singular subject passage» no concuerda con el verbo «produce», que está en plural. «An island and the mainland shore» es un complemento compuesto en plural de la preposición «between» y no el sujeto. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «produce» por «produces».
questions.sentence: The narrow passage between an island and the mainland shore frequently produce whirlpools.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The **<u>narrow</u>** passage between an island **<u>and</u>** the mainland **<u>shore</u>** frequently **<u>produce</u>** whirlpools.

questions.explanation: Being → be: El verbo auxiliar modal «will» va seguido del participio presente «being». Un verbo modal debe ir seguido de la forma básica del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «being» por «be».
questions.sentence: Maryland farmers with land fronting rivers and streams will this year being offered cash to leave fields fallow in hopes of decreasing water pollution.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Maryland **<u>farmers</u>** with land fronting rivers and streams will this year **<u>being</u>** offered cash to leave fields fallow in hopes **<u>of</u>** **<u>decreasing</u>** water pollution.

questions.explanation: Is → be: El verbo auxiliar modal «may» va seguido de la forma de tercera persona del singular de «is». Un verbo modal debe ir seguido de la forma básica del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «is» por «be».
questions.sentence: Today's newer personal computer may more or less indefinitely is left on without suffering any damage.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Today's **<u>newer</u>** personal computer may more or less indefinitely **<u>is</u>** **<u>left</u>** **<u>on</u>** without suffering any damage.

questions.explanation: Helps → help: El verbo auxiliar modal «should» va seguido de la forma de tercera persona del singular «helps». Un verbo modal debe ir seguido de la forma básica del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «helps» por «help».
questions.sentence: A five-year national study will test whether a brain exercise should with time helps healthy older people avoid Alzheimer's disease.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A five-year national study **<u>will</u>** test **<u>whether</u>** a brain exercise should with time **<u>helps</u>** healthy older people **<u>avoid</u>** Alzheimer's disease.

questions.explanation: Will → would: Esta frase contiene los verbos en pasado «was...performed» y «was not anticipated», así como el verbo en futuro «will become». El pasado no debe utilizarse con «will». Para corregir esta frase, puedes sustituir «will» por «would».
questions.sentence: In 1743, when Handel's Messiah was first performed to a limited audience at a charity event in Dublin, Ireland, it was not anticipated that it will become a world-renowned oratorio.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>In</u>** 1743, when Handel's Messiah was **<u>first</u>** performed to a limited audience at a charity event in Dublin, Ireland, it **<u>was</u>** not anticipated that it **<u>will</u>** become a world-renowned oratorio.

questions.explanation: Would be → will be: Esta frase contiene los verbos «are» y «are» en presente, junto con el verbo condicional «would be». El presente no debe utilizarse con «would». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «would be» por «will be».
questions.sentence: There are currently no more than 200 Siberian tigers left in the wild, and conservation biologists predict that unless drastic measures are taken, there would be fewer than 50 remaining by the year 2010.
questions.sentenceFormatted: There are currently **<u>no more than</u>** 200 Siberian tigers **<u>left</u>** in the wild, and conservation biologists predict **<u>that unless</u>** drastic measures are taken, there **<u>would be</u>** fewer than 50 remaining by the year 2010.

questions.explanation: Unexpectedly shot → was unexpectedly shot: Esta frase incluye el verbo «shot» en voz activa, cuando lo que se necesita es un verbo en voz pasiva. Se necesita un verbo en voz pasiva porque el sujeto «he» debería ser el destinatario de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «unexpectedly shot» por «was unexpectedly shot».
questions.sentence: Theodore Roosevelt went ahead with a scheduled speech after he unexpectedly shot in the chest in Milwaukee in 1912.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Theodore Roosevelt **<u>went</u>** **<u>ahead</u>** with a **<u>scheduled</u>** speech after he **<u>unexpectedly shot</u>** in the chest in Milwaukee in 1912.

questions.explanation: Issued → was issued: Esta frase contiene la expresión pasiva «issued by», que está mal construida. Un verbo en pasivo requiere una forma del verbo auxiliar «be». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «issued» por «was issued».
questions.sentence: The landmark Brown vs. Board of Education of Topeka ruling, which declared that racially segregated public schools were inherently unequal, issued by the Supreme Court on May 17, 1954.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The landmark Brown vs. Board of Education of Topeka ruling, which **<u>declared</u>** that racially **<u>segregated</u>** public schools **<u>were</u>** inherently unequal, **<u>issued</u>** by the Supreme Court on May 17, 1954.

questions.explanation: Laying → laid: Esta frase incluye el verbo en activo «was...laying», cuando lo que se necesita es un verbo en pasivo. Se necesita un verbo en pasivo porque el sujeto «cornerstone» debe ser el destinatario de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «laying» por «laid».
questions.sentence: On October 13, 1792, the cornerstone of the executive mansion, later known as the White House, was carefully laying during a ceremony in the District of Columbia.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>On</u>** October 13, 1792, the cornerstone of the executive mansion, later **<u>known</u>** **<u>as</u>** the White House, was carefully **<u>laying</u>** during a ceremony in the District of Columbia.

questions.explanation: Launching → launched: Esta frase incluye el verbo en activo «was...launching» cuando se necesita un verbo en pasivo. Se necesita un verbo en pasivo porque el sujeto «quest» debe ser el destinatario de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «launching» por «launched».
questions.sentence: Vice President George Bush's quest for the Republican presidential nomination was ceremoniously launching in Houston.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Vice President George **<u>Bush's</u>** quest **<u>for</u>** the Republican **<u>presidential</u>** nomination was ceremoniously **<u>launching</u>** in Houston.

questions.explanation: Opening → opened: Esta frase incluye el verbo en activo «was...opening», cuando lo que se necesita es un verbo en pasivo. Se necesita un verbo en pasivo porque el sujeto debe ser el destinatario de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «opening» por «opened».
questions.sentence: In 1892, the first long-distance telephone line between Chicago and New York was formally opening.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In 1892, the first **<u>long-distance</u>** telephone line **<u>between</u>** Chicago and New York was **<u>formally</u>** **<u>opening</u>**.

questions.explanation: Described → was described: Esta frase incluye el verbo en activo «described» cuando se necesita un verbo en pasivo. Se necesita un verbo en pasivo porque el sujeto debe ser el destinatario de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «described» por «was described».
questions.sentence: An area of thinned ozone covering nearly 8.5 million square miles, about the same area as in the two previous years, described in the latest reports.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>An</u>** area of thinned ozone **<u>covering</u>** nearly 8.5 million square miles, about the same area **<u>as in</u>** the two previous years, **<u>described</u>** in the latest reports.

questions.explanation: Are → is: El sujeto «the singular subject factor» no concuerda con el verbo «are», que está en plural. «Deserts» es el complemento en plural de la preposición «of» y no el sujeto. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «are» por «is».
questions.sentence: A factor in the formation of deserts are high mountains, which shield the desert region from rainfall.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A factor in the formation of deserts **<u>are</u>** high mountains, which **<u>shield</u>** the desert **<u>region</u>** from **<u>rainfall</u>**.

questions.explanation: Despite → although: La preposición despite debe ir seguida de un sustantivo o de un gerundio (-ing), no de una oración completa. La estructura correcta sería Despite being the dominant entertainment medium... o Although television is....
questions.sentence: Despite television is the dominant entertainment medium for United States households, Garrison Keillor’s Saturday night radio show of folk songs and stories is heard by millions of people.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Despite</u>** television is the dominant entertainment medium for United States households, Garrison Keillor’s Saturday night **<u>radio show</u>** of folk songs and stories **<u>is</u>** heard by **<u>millions</u>** of people.

questions.explanation: As many as → as much as: La expresión as many as se utiliza únicamente con sustantivos contables plurales. Como income es un sustantivo incontable, la estructura correcta es As much as 50 percent of the income....
questions.sentence: As many as 50 percent of the income from motion pictures produced in the United States comes from marketing the films abroad.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>As many as</u>** 50 percent of the income from motion pictures **<u>produced</u>** in the United States **<u>comes from</u>** marketing the films **<u>abroad</u>**.

questions.explanation: Near → next: Cuando se habla de un período aproximado de tiempo, se utiliza la expresión the next + período de tiempo. La forma correcta es within the next 50 years.
questions.sentence: Exploration of the Solar System is continuing, and at the present rate of progress all the planets will have been contacted within the near 50 years.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Exploration of the Solar System is **<u>continuing</u>**, and at the present rate of **<u>progress</u>** all the planets will have been contacted **<u>within</u>** the **<u>near</u>** 50 years.

questions.explanation: As → for: La expresión fija es be known for, que significa "ser conocido por". La preposición correcta es for: well known for her large paintings.
questions.sentence: American painter Georgia 0’Keeffe is well known as her large paintings of flowers in which single blossoms are presented as if in close-up.
questions.sentenceFormatted: American painter Georgia 0’Keeffe is well known **<u>as</u>** her large paintings of flowers **<u>in which</u>** single **<u>blossoms</u>** are **<u>presented</u>** as if in close-up.

questions.explanation: During → Although: Se necesita un conector de contraste, no una preposición de tiempo.
questions.sentence: During parasocial relationships still remain one-sided, they have transformed into more interactive environments, allowing individuals to communicate with their personas.
