questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>The</u>** New York Stock Exchange **<u>was began</u>** by brokers who **<u>were</u>** meeting under a tree **<u>located</u>** on what is now Wall Street.

questions.explanation: Banned → were banned: Esta frase incluye el verbo «banned» en forma activa, cuando lo que se necesita es un verbo en forma pasiva. Se necesita un verbo en forma pasiva porque el sujeto «edulcorantes» debe ser el destinatario de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «banned» por «were banned».
questions.sentence: Artificial sweeteners known as cyclamates banned because of evidence that they caused cancer in laboratory rats.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Artificial</u>** sweeteners **<u>known</u>** as cyclamates **<u>banned</u>** because of evidence that they caused cancer in **<u>laboratory</u>** rats.

questions.explanation: Consider → are considered: Esta frase incluye el verbo «consider» en voz activa cuando se necesita un verbo en voz pasiva. Se necesita un verbo en voz pasiva porque los sujetos «source...», «water...» y «...molecules» deben ser los destinatarios de la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «consider» por «are considered».
questions.sentence: An energy source, liquid water, and organic molecules consider the three ingredients essential for life.
questions.sentenceFormatted: An **<u>energy</u>** source, liquid water, and organic **<u>molecules</u>** **<u>consider</u>** the three ingredients essential **<u>for</u>** life.

questions.explanation: Used → are used: En esta frase se utiliza el verbo en activo cuando se debería emplear el verbo en pasivo. Se necesita el verbo en pasivo porque el pronombre sujeto «they» debería recibir la acción del verbo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «used» por «are used».
questions.sentence: Lithium batteries are extremely reliable, so they used to power military radios, pacemakers, watches, and memory backups for computers.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Lithium batteries **<u>are</u>** extremely reliable, **<u>so</u>** they **<u>used</u>** to power military radios, pacemakers, watches, and **<u>memory</u>** backups for computers.

questions.explanation: Few → little: «Material» es un sustantivo incontable cuando significa información o contenido. Por lo tanto, debe usarse «little material», no «few material«. «Few» se usa con sustantivos contables plurales.
questions.sentence: Nathaniel Hawthorne often complained of how few material his life provided for his fiction.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Nathaniel Hawthorne **<u>often</u>** complained of how **<u>few</u>** material his life **<u>provided</u>** for his **<u>fiction</u>**.

questions.explanation: Specialization → specialized: Se necesita un adjetivo para modificar parts.
questions.sentence: The raw material of perception for all the senses consists of neural impulses which are channeled to differently specialization parts of the brain.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The raw material of **<u>perception</u>** for all the senses **<u>consists</u>** of neural impulses **<u>which are</u>** channeled to differently **<u>specialization</u>** parts of the brain.

questions.explanation: Herself → her: Antes del sustantivo contributions se necesita un adjetivo posesivo.
questions.sentence: Mealii Kalama, creator of over 400 Hawaiian quilts, was granted a National Heritage Fellowship in 1985 for herself contributions to folk art.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Mealii Kalama, creator of **<u>over</u>** 400 Hawaiian quilts, **<u>was granted</u>** a National Heritage Fellowship in 1985 for **<u>herself</u>** **<u>contributions</u>** to folk art.

questions.explanation: Such the → such as: La expresión fija para dar un ejemplo es such as. La estructura correcta es such as the three-spined stickleback, que introduce un ejemplo de una especie de pez.
questions.sentence: In some species of fish, such the three-spined stickleback, the male, not the female, performs the task of caring for the young.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In **<u>some</u>** species of fish, **<u>such the</u>** three-spined stickleback, the male, not the female, **<u>performs</u>** the task of **<u>caring</u>** for the young.

questions.explanation: Lightly in weight → light in weight: Después del verbo being, se necesitan adjetivos para describir al sujeto. La expresión correcta es light in weight and remarkably strong.
questions.sentence: The body structure that developed in birds over millions of years is well designed for flight, being both lightly in weight and remarkably strong.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>The</u>** body structure that developed in birds over **<u>millions of</u>** years is well designed for flight, being both **<u>lightly in weight</u>** and **<u>remarkably strong</u>**.

questions.explanation: Well → good: Un adverbio modifica a un adjetivo, sense es un sustantivo por lo que debe cambiarse «well» por «good». La expresión correcta es «a good sense of smell.»
questions.sentence: The dachshund is a hardy, alert dog with a well sense of smell.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The dachshund **<u>is</u>** a hardy, **<u>alert</u>** dog with a **<u>well</u>** sense of **<u>smell</u>**.

questions.explanation: Typical → typically: Cuando un adverbio modifica un participio pasado que funciona como adjetivo, debe utilizarse la forma adverbial. La expresión correcta es «typically more concerned».
questions.sentence: Although they reflect a strong social conscience, Arthur Miller's stage works are typical more concerned with individuals than with systems.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Although</u>** they reflect a strong social conscience, Arthur Miller's stage works are **<u>typical</u>** more **<u>concerned</u>** with individuals than with **<u>systems</u>**.

questions.explanation: Advocacy → advocating: Después de la preposición for, se necesita un sustantivo. La expresión correcta es «known for advocating the interests... o known for advocacy of...».
questions.sentence: Elected to serve in the United States House of Representatives in 1968, Shirley Chisholm was known for advocacy the interests of the urban poor.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Elected **<u>to serve</u>** in the United States House of Representatives in 1968, Shirley Chisholm **<u>was known</u>** for **<u>advocacy</u>** the interests of the **<u>urban</u>** poor.

questions.explanation: In what → in which: Después de una preposición «in», cuando introduce una cláusula relativa, debe utilizarse el pronombre relativo adecuado. La estructura correcta es «in which an observer sees....»
questions.sentence: A mirage is an atmospheric optical illusion in what an observer sees a nonexistent body of water or an image of some object.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A mirage is an **<u>atmospheric</u>** optical illusion **<u>in what</u>** an observer sees a nonexistent body of water **<u>or</u>** an image of some **<u>object</u>**.

questions.explanation: Any of → any other: La respuesta correcta es «any other area». Cuando se hace una comparación dentro de un grupo, se utiliza «any other + sustantivo singular». La frase correcta es «more wheat than any other area of Texas» porque compara una región con todas las demás regiones.
questions.sentence: The Texas Panhandle region, in the northwestern part of the state, produces more wheat, cotton, and grain sorghum than any of other area of Texas.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Texas Panhandle region, **<u>in the</u>** northwestern **<u>part</u>** of the state, produces more wheat, **<u>cotton</u>**, and grain sorghum than **<u>any of</u>** other area of Texas.

questions.explanation: Other → Another: Al referirse a una teoría adicional singular se usa another theory.
questions.sentence: Other theory of gender socialization is that the gender roles and attitudes of older siblings can impact the gender roles adopted by younger children
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Other</u>** theory of gender socialization is that the gender **<u>roles</u>** and attitudes of older siblings can **<u>impact</u>** the gender roles **<u>adopted by</u>** younger children

questions.explanation: Force → forces: La expresión «one of the» requiere un sustantivo plural.
questions.sentence: The attraction of opposite charges is one of the force that keep electrons in orbit around of nucleus of an atom.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The attraction of opposite charges **<u>is</u>** one of the **<u>force</u>** that keep electrons **<u>in orbit</u>** around of nucleus of **<u>an</u>** atom.

questions.explanation: Publish → publishing: La estructura con accumulating, researching, and... requiere paralelismo con gerundios.
questions.sentence: Ornithology, the study of birds is one of the major scientific fields in which amateurs play a role in accumulating, researching, and publish data.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Ornithology, the study of birds is one of the **<u>major</u>** scientific **<u>fields</u>** in which amateurs **<u>play</u>** a role in accumulating, researching, and **<u>publish</u>** data.

questions.explanation: In → From: Para indicar un periodo entre dos años se usa from 1866 to 1883.
questions.sentence: In 1866 to 1883, the bison population in North America was reduced from an estimated 13 million to a few hundred.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>In</u>** 1866 to 1883, the bison population in North America **<u>was reduced</u>** from an **<u>estimated</u>** 13 million to a few **<u>hundred</u>**.

questions.explanation: All of → of all: La estructura correcta es the most widely cultivated of all fruit trees.
questions.sentence: The most widely cultivated all of fruit trees, the apple is second only to the grape in its importance as a temperate-zone fruit
questions.sentenceFormatted: The most widely cultivated **<u>all of</u>** fruit trees, the apple is second **<u>only to</u>** the grape in its **<u>importance</u>** **<u>as</u>** a temperate-zone fruit

questions.explanation: Rest → the rest: Se necesita el artículo definido antes de rest.
questions.sentence: During the Pacific War, several areas, including India, Hawaii, and rest of Australia remained under separate local commands.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>During</u>** the Pacific War, several **<u>areas</u>**, including India, Hawaii, and **<u>rest</u>** of Australia remained **<u>under</u>** separate local commands.

questions.explanation: Few → little: Esta frase incluye el cuantificador contable «few» junto con el sustantivo incontable «water». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «few» por «little».
questions.sentence: Koalas drink so few water that zookeepers become concerned if a koala wants to drink any water.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Koalas drink so **<u>few</u>** water that **<u>zookeepers</u>** become concerned **<u>if</u>** a koala wants **<u>to drink</u>** any water.

questions.explanation: An amount → a number: Esta frase incluye el cuantificador incontable «amount» junto con el sustantivo contable «coins». Para corregir esta frase, puedes sustituir «an amount» por «a number».
questions.sentence: The U.S. national motto, "In God We Trust," first appeared on an amount of coins in 1864.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The U.S. **<u>national</u>** motto, "In God We Trust," first **<u>appeared</u>** on **<u>an amount</u>** of coins **<u>in</u>** 1864.

questions.explanation: Fewer → less: Esta frase incluye el cuantificador contable «fewer» junto con el sustantivo incontable «time». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «fewer» por «less».
questions.sentence: In warmer weather, a caterpillar will spend fewer time in the pupal stage.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>In</u>** warmer **<u>weather</u>**, a caterpillar **<u>will spend</u>** **<u>fewer</u>** time in the pupal stage.

questions.explanation: Much → many: Esta frase incluye el cuantificador incontable «much» junto con el sustantivo contable «climates». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «much» por «many».
questions.sentence: Hummingbirds inhabit much of the world's most extreme climates.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Hummingbirds **<u>inhabit</u>** **<u>much</u>** of the **<u>world's</u>** **<u>most</u>** extreme climates.

questions.explanation: Less → fewer: Esta frase incluye el cuantificador incontable «less» junto con el sustantivo contable «elephants». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «less» por «fewer».
questions.sentence: Because of habitat loss, there are less Asian elephants than African elephants.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Because</u>** of habitat **<u>loss</u>**, there are **<u>less</u>** Asian **<u>elephants</u>** than African elephants.

questions.explanation: Making → doing: El verbo «making» se utiliza con la expresión «the dishes». Con esta expresión se debe emplear una forma del verbo «do». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «making» por «doing».
questions.sentence: The first dishwasher was invented in 1886 by a wealthy woman from Illinois who became very angry at her servants who, when making the dishes, broke many of them.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The first dishwasher was invented in 1886 by a **<u>wealthy</u>** woman from Illinois **<u>who became</u>** very angry at her servants who, when **<u>making</u>** the dishes, **<u>broke</u>** many of them.

questions.explanation: Other → another: El adjetivo «other» se utiliza con la preposición «with». Una preposición requiere un pronombre. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «other» por «another».
questions.sentence: One dolphin can communicate with other by making distinctive underwater sounds.
questions.sentenceFormatted: One dolphin can **<u>communicate</u>** with **<u>other</u>** by **<u>making</u>** distinctive underwater **<u>sounds</u>**.

questions.explanation: Done → made: El verbo «done» se utiliza con la expresión «circuit can be». Con esta expresión se debe emplear una forma del verbo «make». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «done» por «made».
questions.sentence: A simple electric circuit can be done by connecting a battery, a wire, a lightbulb, and a switch.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>A simple</u>** electric **<u>circuit</u>** can be **<u>done</u>** by **<u>connecting</u>** a battery, a wire, a lightbulb, and a switch.

questions.explanation: Alike → like: El adjetivo «alike» se utiliza con el sustantivo «leaves». La preposición «like» debe ir acompañada de un sustantivo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «alike» por «like».
questions.sentence: Many insects like the butterfly, try to look alike leaves during their vulnerable chrysalis stage.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Many</u>** insects **<u>like</u>** the butterfly, try to look **<u>alike</u>** leaves during **<u>their</u>** vulnerable chrysalis stage.

questions.explanation: Other → other: El pronombre «others» se utiliza con el sustantivo «rivers». No se puede utilizar un pronombre con un sustantivo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «others» por «other».
questions.sentence: Compared to the others rivers of the world, the Nile in northern Africa is the longest, and the Amazon River in South America has the most water.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Compared</u>** to the **<u>others</u>** rivers **<u>of the</u>** world, the Nile in northern Africa is the longest, and the Amazon River in South America has **<u>the most</u>** water.

questions.explanation: Another → other: El adjetivo en singular «another» se utiliza con el sustantivo plural «kinds». El adjetivo en plural debe ir acompañado de un sustantivo plural. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «another» por «other».
questions.sentence: Historians know that turkey and pumpkin were served at the first Thanksgiving dinner, but, according to the records, some another kinds of food such as fowl, venison, watercress, leeks, and berries were also served.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Historians **<u>know that</u>** turkey and pumpkin **<u>were served</u>** at the first Thanksgiving dinner, but, according to the records, some **<u>another</u>** kinds of food such as fowl, venison, watercress, leeks, and berries were **<u>also</u>** served.

questions.explanation: Do → make: El verbo «do» se utiliza con la expresión «their long journey». Con esta expresión debería utilizarse una forma del verbo «make». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «do» por «make».
questions.sentence: Without cars or trains, the first pioneers in America had to use covered wagons to do their long journey west.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Without cars or trains, **<u>the first</u>** pioneers in America had to use **<u>covered</u>** wagons **<u>to do</u>** their long journey **<u>west</u>**.

questions.explanation: Other → another: El pronombre indefinido plural «other» se utiliza con el sustantivo «set», que está en singular. El adjetivo en singular debe ir acompañado de un sustantivo en singular. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «other» por «another».
questions.sentence: The most frequently sung song in the world, "Happy Birthday To You," was actually written with other set of words by the Hill sisters in 1893.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The most frequently **<u>sung song</u>** in the world, "Happy Birthday To You," was actually **<u>written</u>** with **<u>other</u>** **<u>set of</u>** words by the Hill sisters in 1893.

questions.explanation: Does → makes: El verbo «does» se utiliza con la expresión «a very large book». Con esta expresión se debe emplear una forma del verbo «make». Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «does» por «makes».
questions.sentence: An unabridged dictionary of the English language will list more than 600,000 words, a number which does for a very large book indeed.
questions.sentenceFormatted: An **<u>unabridged</u>** dictionary of the English language will list more than 600,000 words, a **<u>number</u>** which **<u>does</u>** for a very large book **<u>indeed</u>**.

questions.explanation: Like → alike: El adjetivo «like» se utiliza en el predicado. Este tipo de adjetivo solo puede ir delante del sustantivo. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «like» por «alike».
questions.sentence: Two experiments were completed in a like fashion, but the results of the experiments were not at all like.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Two **<u>experiments</u>** were completed in a **<u>like</u>** fashion, but the results of the experiments **<u>were</u>** not at all **<u>like</u>**.

questions.explanation: Like → likely: El adjetivo «like» se utiliza para describir el sustantivo «tornados», pero «like» solo puede ir delante de un sustantivo. Para describir el sustantivo se necesita el adjetivo «likely», de formación irregular. Para corregir esta frase, puedes cambiar «like» por «likely».
questions.sentence: National Weather Service forecasters issue a tornado watch for areas where tornadoes are most like to occur.
questions.sentenceFormatted: National Weather Service **<u>forecasters</u>** issue a tornado watch for areas **<u>where</u>** tornadoes **<u>are</u>** most **<u>like</u>** to occur.

questions.explanation: Fifteen → fifteenth: Cuando un siglo está expresado con un número ordinal, este debe llevar el sufijo correspondiente. La expresión correcta es «the late fifteenth century».
questions.sentence: A number of the American Indian languages spoken at the time of the European arrival in the New World in the late fifteen century have become extinct.
questions.sentenceFormatted: A number **<u>of</u>** the American Indian languages **<u>spoken</u>** at the **<u>time</u>** of the European arrival in the New World in the late **<u>fifteen</u>** century have become extinct.

questions.explanation: Después de other, cuando modifica un sustantivo contable, este debe ir en plural. La forma correcta es other types of....
questions.sentence: Electric lamps came into widespread use during the early 1900’s and have replaced other type of fat, gas, or oil lamps for almost every purpose.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Electric lamps came into widespread use during the early 1900’s and **<u>have replaced</u>** other **<u>type</u>** of fat, gas, or **<u>oil</u>** lamps for **<u>almost every</u>** purpose.

questions.explanation: Instead → instead of: La expresión fija es «instead of», utilizada para indicar sustitución o contraste entre dos opciones. Siempre debe incluir la preposición «of».
questions.sentence: During the 1870’s iron workers in Alabama proved they could produce iron by burning iron ore with coke, instead than with charcoal.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>During</u>** the 1870’s iron workers in Alabama proved they **<u>could</u>** produce iron by **<u>burning</u>** iron ore with coke, **<u>instead</u>** than with charcoal.

questions.explanation: Capability → capable: Después del adjetivo «capable», se utiliza la estructura fija «capable of + gerundio». La forma correcta es «capable of secreting calcium.»
questions.sentence: Fossils in 500-inillion-year-old rocks demonstrate that life forms in the Cambrian period were mostly marine animals capability of secreting calcium to form shells.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Fossils in 500-inillion-year-old rocks demonstrate **<u>that</u>** life forms **<u>in</u>** the Cambrian period **<u>were</u>** mostly marine animals **<u>capability</u>** of secreting calcium to form shells.

questions.explanation: Medicinal → medicine: La oración presenta una lista de elementos paralelos: «Energy research, medicine, tourism, and mining». Se necesitan sustantivos, no adjetivos. «Medicinal» significa "relacionado con la medicina", pero no funciona como elemento de la lista.
questions.sentence: Energy research, medicinal, tourism, and copper and molybdenum mining are important to the economy of Butte, Montana.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Energy research, **<u>medicinal</u>**, tourism, and copper and molybdenum **<u>mining</u>** are important **<u>to</u>** the **<u>economy</u>** of Butte, Montana.

questions.explanation: Depth → Deep: Se necesita un adverbio/adjetivo de lugar; deep within indica ubicación a gran profundidad.
questions.sentence: Depth within ancient tombs, 3,000-year-old peanuts have been found alongside mummies.
questions.sentenceFormatted: **<u>Depth</u>** within **<u>ancient</u>** tombs, 3,000-year-old peanuts **<u>have</u>** been found **<u>alongside</u>** mummies.

questions.explanation: Promotion → promote: Después de to se usa el verbo en forma base.
questions.sentence: The Pejman Foundation is an Iranian nonprofit arts foundation, established by Hamidreza Pejman in 2015 to promotion art in a space free of nationality and geographical boundaries.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The Pejman Foundation is **<u>an</u>** Iranian nonprofit **<u>arts</u>** foundation, established by Hamidreza Pejman in 2015 to **<u>promotion</u>** art in a space **<u>free</u>** of nationality and geographical boundaries.

questions.explanation: Endure → endurance: Se requiere un sustantivo para mantener la lista paralela con speed y strength.
questions.sentence: The decathlon requires an athlete to possess the whole spectrum of athletic ability to be successful including speed, strength, and endure.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The decathlon **<u>requires</u>** an athlete to possess the whole spectrum of **<u>athletic</u>** ability to **<u>be successful</u>** including speed, strength, and **<u>endure</u>**.

questions.explanation: Inventor → invention: La frase correcta sería «One invention that Thomas Edison can take credit for is the light bulb», porque se habla de una invención, no de una persona.
questions.sentence: One inventor that Thomas Edison can take credit for is the light bulb.
questions.sentenceFormatted: One **<u>inventor</u>** that Thomas Edison can **<u>take credit</u>** **<u>for</u>** is the light **<u>bulb</u>**.

questions.explanation: Structural → structure: En una enumeración, todos los elementos deben mantener la misma categoría gramatical. La estructura correcta es «eating habits, posture, and skeletal structure», donde todos los elementos son sustantivos.
questions.sentence: Dinosaurs are traditionally classified as cold-blooded reptiles, but recent evidence based on eating habits, posture, and skeletal structural suggests some may have been warm-blooded.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Dinosaurs **<u>are</u>** traditionally classified as cold-blooded reptiles, **<u>but</u>** recent evidence based on eating habits, posture, and skeletal **<u>structural</u>** suggests some **<u>may have been</u>** warm-blooded.

questions.explanation: Severity → severe: Cuando un sustantivo modifica a otro sustantivo, debe utilizarse la forma adjetival del sustantivo. La expresión correcta es «severe business declines», donde «severe» modifica a «business declines».
questions.sentence: Since the Great Depression of the 1930’s, social programs such as Social Security have been built into the economy to help avert severity business declines.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Since the Great Depression of the 1930’s, social **<u>programs</u>** such as Social Security have **<u>been built</u>** into the economy **<u>to help</u>** avert **<u>severity</u>** business declines.

questions.explanation: Widely → wide: La expresión correcta es «a wide range of household products».
questions.sentence: In the 1970’s consumer activities succeeded in promoting laws that set safety standards for automobiles, children’s clothing, and a widely range of household products.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In the 1970’s **<u>consumer</u>** activities **<u>succeeded</u>** in promoting laws that set **<u>safety</u>** standards for automobiles, children’s clothing, and a **<u>widely</u>** range of household products.

questions.explanation: Symbolic → sybolism: En una enumeración, todos los elementos deben pertenecer a la misma categoría gramatical. La estructura correcta es «fact, fiction, adventure, and subtle symbolism», donde todos son sustantivos.
questions.sentence: The works of the author Herman Melville are literary creations of a high order, blending fact, fiction, adventure, and subtle symbolic.
questions.sentenceFormatted: The works of the **<u>author</u>** Herman Melville are **<u>literary</u>** creations of a high order, blending **<u>fact</u>**, fiction, adventure, and subtle **<u>symbolic</u>**.

questions.explanation: Interesting → interest: Después del adjetivo «considerable», se necesita un sustantivo. La forma correcta es «considerable interest».
questions.sentence: In the early twentieth century, there was considerable interesting among sociologists in the fact that in the United States the family was losing its traditional roles.
questions.sentenceFormatted: In the early twentieth century, there was considerable **<u>interesting</u>** among sociologists in the fact **<u>that</u>** in the United States **<u>the family</u>** was losing its **<u>traditional</u>** roles.

questions.explanation: Admiration → admired: Después del verbo «made possible», se utiliza un participio pasado para describir el estado del sustantivo. La expresión correcta es «statues still admired», donde «admired» modifica a «statues».
questions.sentence: Government money appropriated for art in the 1930’s made possible hundreds of murals and statues still admiration in small towns all over the United States.
questions.sentenceFormatted: Government money appropriated **<u>for art</u>** in the 1930’s made possible **<u>hundreds of</u>** murals and statues still **<u>admiration</u>** in small towns **<u>all over</u>** the United States.

questions.explanation: Value → valued: Después del verbo «is», se necesita un participio pasado que funcione como adjetivo. La expresión correcta es «is chiefly valued for its fruit».
questions.sentence: Although the pecan tree is chiefly value for its fruit, its wood is used extensively for flooring, furniture, boxes, and crates.
